subject: TTFT streaming SLO follow-up with DataStride - next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>
To: Chris Nguyen <chris.nguyen@datstride.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@datstride.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: TTFT & streaming SLOs - recap + next steps

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning, Chris - great conversation. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can align on a performance plan:

Summary of requirements (from today's call)
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) target: <= 120 ms for 95th percentile for single-turn requests (interactive chat flows).
- Streaming transport: plan to use SSE for web clients and WebSocket for mobile apps; need consistent chunk cadence and small chunk sizes for UI responsiveness.
- Chunk cadence target: goal of 50-100 ms between chunks for streaming responses when the model is generating; fallback acceptable at 200 ms if bandwidth constrained.
- Throughput expectation: sustained 200 req/sec during peak (US-east), burst to 500 req/sec for short periods.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent active users ~50, peak ~150.
- Response sizes: median 40 tokens, p95 200 tokens.

Immediate next steps
1) I attached a short SLO worksheet (SLO_requirements.xlsx) - please fill in any missing traffic/response numbers and the dev URLs you want us to test against.
2) We'll run a focused TTFT + streaming cadence test from our Dedicated environment (we'll mimic SSE + WebSocket).
3) Marissa will scope the test plan and share the timeline; we expect an initial baseline report in 72 hours after we receive your test endpoints and traffic profile.

Can you confirm the SSE/WebSocket choices above and add any missing traffic numbers in the attached sheet? If fine, we'll schedule the ingestion test for Friday.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Chris Nguyen <chris.nguyen@datstride.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@datstride.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: TTFT & streaming SLOs - recap + next steps

Aditya - thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the details and answered inline:

- TTFT: 95th <= 120 ms is what we need for chat. We can accept 150 ms if it materially reduces cost, but 120 ms is the target.
- Streaming: SSE for desktop/web, WebSocket for mobile is correct. For mobile, we prefer WebSocket to keep connections long-lived.
- Chunk cadence: 75 ms target sounds ideal. If you need us to choose, go with 75 ms target / 200 ms fallback.
- Throughput: 200 req/sec sustained is accurate for our US-east peak. Bursts up to 600 req/sec are possible during promotions.
- Concurrency: concurrent active users ~60 typically, can jump to 180 during peaks.
- Response sizes: median ~45 tokens, p95 ~220 tokens.

I filled the SLO sheet and uploaded to the Drive folder (link above). Please note we have an internal constraint: we must see 99.9% availability for streaming endpoints during the 30-day evaluation period.

Looking forward to the test. If you can pick a test window Friday afternoon (US/Pacific), we'll keep engineering on call.

- Chris Nguyen
Head of AI Platform
DataStride
chris.nguyen@datstride.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Chris Nguyen <chris.nguyen@datstride.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: TTFT & streaming SLOs - recap + next steps

Thanks Chris - great clarifications. I'm looping in the infra team (we'll route tests through our US-east Dedicated pool) and documenting the test plan below. Planned steps:

1) Baseline (no batching, single-connection streaming) - measure cold TTFT and first token latencies across 50 clients.
2) Production-like test (concurrency + batching policies) - emulate 200 req/s sustained with 60 concurrent active clients, then a burst to 600 req/s to validate degraded modes and fallback routing.
3) Streaming cadence validation - test SSE and WebSocket with chunk cadence set to 75 ms and 200 ms to see UI impact and tokenization alignment.
4) Observability/metrics - we'll capture TTFT (p50/p95/p99), per-chunk latency, chunk sizes, throughput, and error budgets. We'll also snapshot KV cache hit rates and batching efficiency.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Test plan + schedule (this afternoon)
- Baseline results (within 48 hours of test run)
- Full report with recommended config (including quantization/batching suggestions) within 72 hours

Question for DataStride: can you provide a short test tokenization hook or an example prompt set we should use (to approximate token cadence)? Also, confirm whether clients will accept frequent small chunks (UX question) - if not, we can tune for larger chunk sizes but that affects TTFT.

I'll schedule the Friday afternoon window at 1:30pm PT unless you prefer 3pm. Aditya, I'll need you to confirm the final window and we'll send a calendar invite and an access token for our Dedicated test harness.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@datstride.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>, Chris Nguyen <chris.nguyen@datstride.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: TTFT & streaming SLOs - recap + next steps

Quick ack from Priya (ops): 1:30pm PT Friday works for our team. We uploaded an example prompt set and tokenization sample to the Drive folder - file name: datastride_prompt_set_v1.json. We prefer smaller chunks for the desktop UI (75 ms cadence), but for mobile we may accept 150-200 ms.

Also, re: availability target - we need 99.9% for streaming during evaluation; please include uptime checks in the test plan. Priya will be on the call for any immediate troubleshooting.

Thanks - see you Friday,
Priya Shah
SRE Manager
DataStride
priya.shah@datstride.com
